hints.content: $\sqrt[3]{125}$ is the number that, when multiplied by itself three times, equals $125$.
If you can't think of that number, you can break down $125$ into its prime factorization and look for equal groups of numbers.

Let's draw a factor tree.

options.alt: A factor tree for one hundred twenty-five. It starts with just the number one hundred twenty-five.
A factor tree for one hundred twenty-five. On hundred twenty-five is the product of five and twenty-five. The five is circled.
A factor tree for one hundred twenty-five. On hundred twenty-five is the product of five and twenty-five. The five is circled. Twenty-five is the product of five and five. The first five is circled.
A factor tree for one hundred twenty-five. On hundred twenty-five is the product of five and twenty-five. The five is circled. Twenty-five is the product of five and five. Both fives are circled.

hints.content: So the prime factorization of $125$ is $5\times 5\times 5$.
We're looking for $\sqrt[3]{125}$, so we want to split the prime factors into three identical groups.
We only have three prime factors, and we want to split them into three groups, so this is easy.
